Plot method for multiScaleR objects

Source: R/plot_method.R
plot.multiScaleR.Rd

Plots the optimized kernel weight distribution for each spatial covariate in a fitted multiScaleR object, with optional annotations showing the effective scale of effect and its 95% confidence interval.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'multiScaleR'
plot(x, dimension = c("2d", "1d"), ...)

Arguments

x

A fitted multiScaleR object returned by multiScale_optim.

dimension

Character. "2d" (default) marks the radius containing the requested proportion of ideal planar kernel weight. "1d" restores the original distance along a line through the point.

...

Optional named arguments to customize the plot:

prob

Numeric between 0 and 1 (exclusive). Cumulative kernel weight enclosed by the marked distance under the selected dimension. Default: 0.9.

scale_dist

Logical. If TRUE (default), a vertical dashed line is drawn at the effective distance, and a shaded rectangle spans the 95% confidence interval.

add_label

Logical. If TRUE (default), a caption below the plot reports sigma, the dimensional definition, the effective distance, and 95% CI bounds (in map units).

Value

A list of ggplot2 objects (one per covariate with a finite scale and effective distance), returned invisibly. Plots are printed as a side effect.

Details

Development versions after 0.7.3 default to 2D reporting, as do kernel_dist and plot_kernel. Set dimension = "1d" to reproduce the original line-based distances. This switch changes distance markers and converted confidence limits, not the fitted sigma, regression coefficients, or likelihood.

The curve shows cell weight declining with distance, normalized over the plotted sample distances. It is not a radial weight distribution. A planar marker accounts for the increasing area of concentric rings, so the area under the displayed curve to its left is not the stated proportion. Distances refer to an ideal untruncated kernel. Actual retained weight can differ with max_D, raster edges, missing cells, and cell geometry.

Hard-radius covariates show a uniform buffer and mark its full radius, regardless of prob or dimension. A shaded interval is drawn only when finite limits are available.

See also

plot_kernel

Examples

# \donttest{
## Using package data
data('pts')
data('count_data')
hab <- terra::rast(system.file('extdata',
                   'hab.tif', package = 'multiScaleR'))

kernel_inputs <- kernel_prep(pts = pts,
                             raster_stack = hab,
                             max_D = 250,
                             kernel = 'gaussian')
#> 
#> No sigma values provided...
#> Creating necessary elements to optimize sigma
#> 
#> Extracting values from raster layers...

mod <- glm(y ~ hab,
           family = poisson,
           data = count_data)

## Optimize scale
opt <- multiScale_optim(fitted_mod = mod,
                        kernel_inputs = kernel_inputs)
#> 
#> 
#> Optimization complete
#> 
#>  WARNING!!!
#>  The estimated scale of effect approaches or exceeds the current search extent.
#>  Consider increasing max_D in `kernel_prep` to >=250.56 to ensure accurate estimation of scale.
#> 
#> 

plot(opt)

plot(opt, dimension = "1d")  # Original line-based distances


plot(opt, prob = 0.95)


plot(opt, scale_dist = FALSE)


plot(opt, scale_dist = TRUE, add_label = FALSE)

# }
